thread_analysis.thread_summary: NEC Platforms (contacts Hidemasa Hashimoto, Kensuke Hayashi, and several other team members including Daisuke Tsuruta, Terumasa Murayama, Wakashi Hoshi, Kei Tanaka) works with Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Masaya Iida) on Bluetooth SIG certification for three Communications Terminal product models sharing the same Bluetooth module and Host Stack. The thread documents a substantial registration-strategy saga: discovering that Google's Fluoride Host Stack series (1.3-1.6) all carry a fatal internal GAP/GATT Consistency Check defect, applying a specific Test Case Waiver (TCW) for Core-layer Invalids caused by adding new profile definitions to unmodified subsystems, a methodical approach to minimizing PTS test scope by reusing inherited ICS values where gaps don't matter, registration form handling for multiple product names, and final Review Page confirmation pending the customer's internal wire transfer approval process.
all_questions_found: Can Google's Fluoride Host Stack (versions 1.3-1.6) be combined with our module for this registration? (see thread_0250_case_01)
How do we avoid Core-layer Invalid errors from adding new profile definitions without modifying our referenced subsystems? (see thread_0250_case_02)
Which specific profiles need new PTS testing versus which can inherit the reference registration's ICS, and is there a simpler ICS comparison method? (see thread_0250_case_03)
How should three distinct product model names be entered, and what happens to the registration's Design Name? (see thread_0250_case_04)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread demonstrates a comprehensive registration-strategy methodology: diagnosing an inherent defect in a proposed Host Stack series via preliminary Consistency Check before committing to it, applying a specific named TCW exception for Core-layer Invalids arising purely from profile additions, minimizing PTS test scope by classifying each ICS gap as either acceptable (reuse inherited value) or non-negotiable (requires new test report), and correctly structuring a multi-model registration's Design Name.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Across this thread, Allion's approach consistently favored diagnosing root causes precisely (preliminary Consistency Check trials, ICS-item-by-item gap classification) before committing to costly remediation paths (full retesting, subsystem modification), and proactively flagged registration-site mechanics (TCW applicability, Design Name defaulting) that aren't self-evident from the site's own interface.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See thread_0250_case_01 through thread_0250_case_04 for the specific risks of each question.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion's preliminary trial-project diagnostics caught the Fluoride Host Stack defect before the customer committed registration fees to a combination that couldn't succeed, and the TCW/ICS-gap-classification approach avoided unnecessary full-scope retesting.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For complex multi-model registrations referencing third-party Host Stack series, run preliminary trial-project Consistency Checks before committing to a specific reference combination, know the relevant TCW catalog for common Core-layer Invalid scenarios (like adding profiles to unmodified subsystems), and minimize PTS test scope by classifying each ICS gap as negotiable or non-negotiable rather than defaulting to full retesting or blind inheritance.
